the serum Spec fPL and 1, 2‐o‐ dilauryl‐ rac‐glycero ‐ 3‐glutarate‐(6’‐methylresorfine) ester ( DGGR) lipase assays have limited agreement with histologic inflammation of the feline pancreas.
the sensitivity and specificity of Spec fPL and serum DGGR for antemortem pancreatitis in cats are both low and that the agreement between these 2 tests is poor.
both Spec fPL and serum DGGR assays performed similarly, but both tests were limited by low sensitivity for detection of pancreatic inflammation.

the Spec fPL or the DGGR assay cannot be recommended as a single test to diagnose or rule out pancreatitis in cats.
the Spec fPL test and DGGR assay have limited diagnostic value for the diagnosis of pancreatitis.
neither the Spec fPL nor the DGGR assay can be considered a reliable test to rule‐out pancreatitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both Spec fPL and lipase activity were useful in the detection of pancreatic inflammation, but that the sensitivity of both tests was low.
both tests have a high specificity but low sensitivity.
the Spec fPL test is a useful test for antemortem detection of pancreatitis in the cat but that it is not as specific as previously thought.

neither lipase assay can be used as a sole criterion to diagnose pancreatitis in cats.
the histologic grading scheme we employed may be too sensitive to detect mild pancreatic inflammation.
the Spec fPL test is not a good test to rule in or rule out the diagnosis of pancreatitis.
